explanation: Store one character per trie edge and mark terminal nodes. Insertion creates missing edges. Exact search requires a terminal marker. Prefix search requires a matching path and at least one stored word, so the empty prefix is false before any insertion, as this collection specifies.
timeComplexity: O(L) expected time per operation for word or prefix length L. Following or creating a path performs one expected constant-time child lookup per character.
spaceComplexity: O(T) stored trie nodes across all insertions; O(1) extra per search. One node is created per new prefix; a search holds only its current node reference.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every trie path spells exactly its edge characters, and a terminal marker denotes an inserted complete word. Insertion creates only the needed path and marks its endpoint. Exact search checks the terminal marker, while prefix search checks a path and the collection’s nonempty-word-set condition. Those rules distinguish an inserted word from a mere prefix.
walkthrough: Before insertion, startsWith("") is false in this collection. Insert "mint": startsWith("mi") becomes true, but search("mi") is still false. Insert "mi", after which search("mi") is true. Query results are [false,true,false,true]. The arrays describe calls on one instance in order; expected contains only Search/StartsWith boolean results, omitting Insert returns.
edgeCases: Prefix search and exact search are different operations.
Reinserting the same word does not duplicate it.
The empty prefix is false before any insertion.
